name: GemOx (Gemcitabine / Oxaliplatin)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Non-cross-resistant doublet for multiply-relapsed, platinum-refractory germ cell tumor after failure of first-line cisplatin-based chemotherapy and salvage (conventional or high-dose). Paclitaxel may be added (GOP) at physician discretion. Serum tumor markers track response. In our own words for a DRAFT decision-support tool.

histology: germ cell tumor (seminoma and nonseminomatous germ cell tumor / NSGCT), platinum-refractory

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis (moderate emetic risk)
premedications.notes: Oxaliplatin-containing doublet; provide prophylaxis per the standard emetic-risk framework.

supportiveCare: Cold sensitivity counselling: oxaliplatin causes cold-induced acute dysesthesias; avoid cold food/drink and cold exposure around infusion.
Neuropathy: monitor cumulative oxaliplatin peripheral sensory neuropathy; consider dose reduction or holiday.
Myelosuppression: gemcitabine plus oxaliplatin is myelosuppressive; assess febrile-neutropenia risk and consider G-CSF support.
Paclitaxel may be added as a third agent (GOP) in fit patients; if used, add taxane premedication and monitor for neuropathy and hypersensitivity.
monitoring: Serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) before each cycle and at restaging
Peripheral neuropathy assessment each cycle - oxaliplatin
Liver and renal function before each cycle

doseModificationRules.text: Review required; reduce oxaliplatin, hold, or introduce a treatment holiday. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: ANC < 1000 or platelets < 100k on treatment day
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; delay or reduce per institutional criteria. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.notes: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on Days 1 and 8, every 21 days. Non-cross-resistant partner used in platinum-refractory germ cell tumor salvage. Dose and schedule in our own words from standard later-line practice (general references NCCN/DeVita).

drugs.name: Oxaliplatin
drugs.notes: Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 IV on Day 1, every 21 days. Cold-induced acute neuropathy and cumulative sensory neuropathy expected; counsel on cold avoidance. Dose and schedule in our own words from standard later-line practice (general references NCCN/DeVita).
